claims.text: The initial material is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The proposed intervention is partial substitution of Mo with Nb.
Nb is a lighter refractory-element substitute for Mo.
Partial substitution of Mo with Nb will reduce the density of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Partial substitution of Mo with Nb will not significantly compromise room-temperature mechanical performance.
Partial substitution of Mo with Nb will not significantly compromise high-temperature mechanical performance.
Grain size and phase composition mediate the mechanical response of the modified alloy.
Mo-to-Nb substitution will maintain a microstructure and phase composition similar to those of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
Maintaining similar microstructure and phase composition will preserve mechanical properties.
The modified alloy will have at least 5% lower density than as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
The modified alloy will retain room-temperature yield strength above 1500 MPa.
The modified alloy will retain yield strength above 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The modified alloy's room-temperature fracture toughness will improve or remain comparable to the baseline.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of about 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has an elevated-temperature yield strength of 855 MPa.
Mechanical testing will be conducted under uniaxial tension at room temperature and 1000 °C.
Alloys spanning varying degrees of Mo-to-Nb substitution will be prepared and compared through density and mechanical measurements.
Tensile tests can provide the proposed room-temperature fracture-toughness measurement.
Prior RHEA work found that replacing high-density refractory elements with lower-density refractory elements produced lower-density alloys that retained strong high-temperature properties.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis allows that only an unknown optimal Mo-to-Nb substitution level may work, but the rule declares the whole hypothesis falsified if any member of the varied-composition series fails a threshold. A nonoptimal variant can therefore reject a hypothesis that only predicts success for some optimized substitution.

The experiment specifies tensile testing to evaluate fracture toughness but does not specify a fracture-mechanics specimen, precrack, geometry, or toughness protocol, so the stated loading plan does not operationalize the claimed fracture-toughness measurement.
